title: Week in review
prompt:
This is the weekly review, a scheduled run, and the user is not present. They asked for one look each
week at {assets}: what the week changed, what is due next, and which earlier findings it bore out.

For each asset, find what was filed, reported or announced this week and how its price and the measures
behind the user's reasons and lines moved. Prefer the filing or the company's own release; a news report
stands in only with its publisher and date. Give each item its date and source link, keep the publication
date apart from the event date, and say in a sentence what the week means for the reasons and lines the
user wrote for that asset. Then name what is due in the next two weeks that bears on those reasons, such as
results, a shareholder meeting, a dividend date or a data release. Then say which earlier findings this
week bore out or overturned, such as a line reading on the asset's page or what last week's review
reported (previous_run). Name each asset you could not check.

Report facts and what they mean for the user's reasons and lines; give no call to buy, sell, hold or
resize and no target of your own. This review reports every week, a quiet week in a few lines.
Answer in {language}.
